title: A Veil for the Ember
premise: Ines Oyelaran, last apprentice of the Veilwright Guild—a smugglers' brotherhood that once ferried refugees out of the drowned kingdom of Sarel—finds her world upended when a mute child arrives speaking Old Sareli, a language that died with the kingdom itself. Hunted by the Crown's Ashcarts, who burned the Guild's records and mean to burn its last members too, Ines must relearn the guild's forgotten craft: not smuggling goods, but smuggling people across the veil into a country that no longer exists on any map. Guided by the child, who remembers Sarel from the inside, and betrayed by the mentor who sold the Guild's secrets to survive, Ines discovers the door out can only be opened by someone willing to give up their own name and history as toll. In the end, Ines pays that price—becoming the new doorkeeper, nameless and bound—while the child and the Guild's scattered survivors pass through to a Sarel reborn beyond the winter, leaving Ines a legend the smugglers' roads will never forget.
about_author: Wendell Dunmore is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade drawing borders for governments before turning to stories about the people borders fail. They live in a drafty house full of obsolete maps and write about doors, debts, and the geography of forgetting.

chapters.title: The Last Tollbooth
chapters.summary: Ines Oyelaran's POV. Ines runs a final smuggling job through the Thornfell passes for the near-extinct Veilwright Guild, dodging Crown patrols and reflecting on the guild's decay. She returns to the guildhall to find it nearly empty. Emotional beat: weary pride in a craft that is dying with her masters.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. During a snowstorm, a mute child appears at the guildhall door, half-frozen, speaking a language no one recognizes—until the guild's oldest member, Maren, goes pale: it is Old Sareli. Emotional beat: unease blooming into wonder and dread.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals the Veilwrights were once more than smugglers: they moved refugees through the veil into Sarel before it fell. The records were burned by the Crown's Ashcarts, but Maren kept one stolen page. Emotional beat: guilt over decades of silence.

chapters.title: Ashcarts at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ashcart inquisitors arrive searching for the child, whom they call 'the Remnant.' Ines hides the child in the smugglers' hollow beneath the floorboards and lies for the first time to a Crown officer. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Language of Doors
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The child, whom Ines names Ember, begins teaching Ines fragments of Old Sareli, and Ines realizes the guild's old road-songs were veiled instructions. Emotional beat: the thrill of inheritance—she is more her guild's daughter than she knew.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Debt
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin, Ines's mentor, secretly meets an Ashcart handler, revealing he sold the Guild's routes years ago to buy his own survival—and now they want the child in exchange for his pardon. Emotional beat: self-loathing dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Flight into Thornfell
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Warned by a smuggler's signal-fire, Ines flees with Ember and Maren into the high passes as the first true snow of the long winter falls. Emotional beat: grief for the guildhall, left burning behind them.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines navigates a smuggler's road that only opens to the old songs, and Ember's presence makes the hidden waymarks glow. The veil between worlds is thinner than anyone believed. Emotional beat: awe tempered by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Grave
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. At an abandoned waystation, Maren confesses she was the last person ferried out of Sarel—and that she left her sister behind. She believes Ember is a message from the drowned kingdom. Emotional beat: grief finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Hounds of the Ash
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ashcart trackers with ash-hounds corner them in a ravine; Ines collapses a smuggler's bridge to escape, nearly losing Ember to the river. Emotional beat: terror, and the first hint she would die for the child.

chapters.title: Corvin's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin catches up under a flag of truce, offering Ines a deal: hand over Ember, and the Crown grants the Guild a pardon and its roads back. He genuinely believes he is saving them. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of survival.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pardon
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines refuses, and Corvin leaves with the Guild's route-book, meaning every hidden road is now Crown property. Maren falls ill in the deepening cold. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Ember Speaks
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Ember finally speaks in the common tongue, revealing they are the last soul who walked out of Sarel before the veil sealed—and the door can only be reopened from the outside by a doorkeeper's sacrifice. Emotional beat: the terrible weight of being a key.

chapters.title: The Doorkeeper's Toll
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ember explains the toll: the door opens only for one who surrenders their name, memories, and claim to the world. Ines begins quietly putting her affairs in order without telling anyone. Emotional beat: quiet, resolute dread.

chapters.title: Winter's Verge
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren, dying, teaches Ines the final verses of the door-song and gives her the stolen page—the map to the First Door beneath Thornfell's heart. Emotional beat: a passing of the flame between generations.

chapters.title: The Trap at the First Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the door beneath the mountain, Corvin and the Ashcarts are waiting, having followed Maren's page. Ember is seized; Ines is beaten and left bound as the Ashcarts prepare to seal the door with fire. Emotional beat: despair at the bottom of the fall.

chapters.title: The Song Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Bound beside Ines, Ember sings the door-song, and the mountain answers—the First Door wakes, and the Ashcarts' fire becomes fuel for its opening. Emotional beat: hope kindled in captivity.

chapters.title: What Corvin Carried
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Confronted by the living door and the child's fearlessness, Corvin breaks: he turns on the Ashcart commander to buy Ines a moment, paying for a lifetime of sold secrets. Emotional beat: redemption bought too late to enjoy.

chapters.title: The Toll Is Paid
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the threshold, Ines speaks her renunciation—her name, her roads, her history—as toll, and the door opens onto a Sarel reborn under a gentler sky. Ember and the survivors of the Guild's scattered families cross. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Doorkeeper
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, nameless now. Ines takes up station as the new doorkeeper, bound to the threshold, watching Ember's small figure vanish into the light. The winter closes over Thornfell, but the door holds. Emotional beat: sorrow braided with peace.

chapters.title: Roads Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Epistolary/omniscient POV. Years later, smugglers tell of a door in the high passes that opens for those who sing the old songs, and of a faceless keeper who lets the hunted pass and turns the hunters away. Emotional beat: legend outliving the person.

chapters.title: A Veil for the Ember
chapters.summary: Ember's POV, grown. On the far side, Ember—now Sarel's first historian of the crossing—sings the door-song at their own door and, for one breath, hears a voice answer in a smuggler's accent. Emotional beat: the closing of the circle; love outlasting name and veil.
